Area Forecast Discussion...UPDATED
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
704 PM PDT Thu Oct 29 2026

.SYNOPSIS...29/704 PM.

Rain chances continue through much of the weekend, with the peak
of the rain likely occuring Saturday night evening into Sunday 
morning. Warmer and drier conditions expected early next week, 
with the potetnial for more light rain by the middle of next week.

&&

.SHORT TERM (THU-SUN)...29/704 PM.

***UPDATE***

A cool and cloudy day across the forecast area saw high
temperatures generally around a few degrees cooler compared to
yesterday. Some very light sprinkles fell across the area with a 
few areas recording one hundredth of an inch, including here at 
the office in Oxnard. All eyes turn to what should be a relatively
beneficial rainfall through Halloween weekend, however, even 
light rain may disrupt outdoor Halloween plans. The forecast 
remains on track with light showers possible through Saturday 
morning and the potential for more steady rain with higher rain 
totals Saturday afternoon/evening into Sunday morning.

***From Previous Discussion***

For the short term, main focus remains on rain chances across the
district. Models continue to be on the same broad synoptic page,
but differ in the details. An upper low will continue to spin off
the Pacific Northwest coast through Saturday, before moving inland
on Sunday. This will result in a very sharp trough, or a weak
upper low, impacting the area this weekend.

Overall, the last couple of model runs have trended a bit "drier"
and further south with this storm, but ensembles, especially the
ECMWF suite, still indicate a decent number of moderate to heavy
rainfall members. So, at this time, there is high confidence in
widespread rainfall across the area, but only moderate confidence
in amounts through the Halloween weekend.

Today through Saturday morning, there will be some scattered light
showers just about anywhere with a deep moist layer in place
across the area. Rainfall totals, if any, through Saturday morning
will be on the order of a few hundredths of an inch. By Saturday
afternoon/evening, the main storm will move eastward towards
Southern California, moving inland during the day on Sunday. As
alluded to above, the heaviest rainfall Saturday night and Sunday
looks to remain south of LA county. Current rainfall totals look 
to generally be in the 0.25 to 1.00 inch range across the area 
with locally higher amounts (up to 2.00 inches) possible across 
favored mountain slopes. Given the continued uncertainty between
models, there still is a 20% chance of amounts about double the
expected totals and a 20% chance of amounts about one half of the
expected totals. 

As for rain rates, the best instability looks to remain south of
LA county. So, rainfall rates are expected to be in the 0.10 to
0.33 inch/hour range. Additionally, any thunderstorm threat looks
to be minimal (under a 10% chance).

.LONG TERM (MON-THU)...29/1255 PM.

For the extended, latest models are exhibiting good synoptic
agreement through the period. At upper levels, ridge will develop
over the area Monday/Tuesday then will shift eastward as a upper
low sweeps northeastward across northern California on Wednesday
and Thursday. At the surface, weak offshore flow will prevail on
Monday/Tuesday with a return of weak onshore flow by Wednesday and
Thursday.

Forecast-wise, the above synoptic pattern will result in benign
weather for the area. With the ridge overhead and weak offshore
pressure gradients, Monday and Tuesday will be dry and warmer with
high temperatures topping out in the upper 60s and 70s. There will
be some northeasterly winds, due to the offshore pressure
gradients, but any winds are expected to remain below advisory
levels. 

For Wednesday and Thursday, a slight cooling trend can be expected
with some increase in high clouds. With the upper low moving
northeast into northern California, there will be a low chance
(less than 20%) of some light showers across the Central Coast.

&&

.AVIATION...29/2313Z.

At 2212Z at KLAX, there was a deep moist layer to 5500 feet. 
marine layer was 5000 ft deep. The top of the inversion was at 
8000 ft with a temperature of 10 C.

High confidence in VFR TAFs for KPMD & KWJF.

Moderate to high confidence in TAFs with VFR cigs for remaining 
sites, with infrequent periods of 020-030 MVFR cigs. Additionally,
there is 10-25% chance of -DZ or -SHRA from late tonight through 
the TAF period.

KLAX...Moderate to high confidence in TAF. VFR cigs likely 
with infrequent periods of BKN020-030 cigs. 15-25% chance of -DZ
or -SHRA from around 30/06Z through the period. Any east wind 
component is expected to remain under 8 kt.

KBUR...Moderate to high confidence in TAF. VFR cigs likely 
with infrequent periods of BKN020-030 cigs. 10-20% chance of -DZ 
or -SHRA from around 30/06Z through the period. No wind issues 
expected.

&&

.MARINE...29/142 PM.

Conditions are expected to remain below Small Craft Advisory 
(SCA) levels through Saturday. Southwest flow aloft will produce 
chances for drizzle and isolated light rain showers Today & Friday.

A storm system is expected to impact the coastal waters this weekend.
However, guidance continues to shift to the south with some solutions
showing the bulk of showers only as far north as the Channel islands.
Regardless, there will be some gusty SCA NW winds behind the system
on Sunday.

&&
